District Ajmer, Rajasthan, involving Mahindra Bolero Pikup bearing registration no. Rj42-Ga-2363

2. The concise material facts relevant to decide the present claim are that on 06.10.2019, deceased

The issue wise determination is as under:-
8.
For the purpose of this issue, the testimony of PW1 Sh. Sumit (alleged eyewitness) is relevant.

He deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit (Ex. PW2/A) that on 06.10.2019 at about 10:15 AM, he alongwith MACP No. 201/20; FIR No. 342/19 DOD: 13.08.2024 his elder brother Prashant Mehta (deceased herein) were going to Ajmer from Jaipur on their respective motorcycles.
He further deposed that they left Jaipur at around 8:30 AM for Ajmer.

He further deposed that his brother Prashant Mehta was driving his motorcycle bearing no. DL3S-ED-9607 very carefully at a normal speed on the extreme left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and approx 25-30 meters ahead of his motorcycle.

He further deposed that at about 10:15 AM, when they reached at Ajmer Road, 100 meters prior to Railway Line, PS. Madanganj, District Ajmer, a Mahindra Bolero Pikup bearing registration no. RJ42-GA-2363 came from front side/wrong side in a rash and negligent manner without following the traffic norms and hit the motorcycle of Prashant Mehta from front side by its front side/driver side with great impact.
He further deposed that the impact was so powerful that Prashant Mehta fell down on the road alongwith motorcycle and sustained grievous/dangerous injuries on his body.
He further deposed that after seeing this, he immediately stopped his motorcycle and ran towards his brother Prashant Mehta.

He further deposed that on shouting by him, the respondent no. 1 stopped his vehicle 20-25 meters away from the place of accident and came to see the injured, however, after seeing the condition of injured, he Mini Mehta And Ors vs Mohammed Ashfaq Assam And Anr on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163157675/

He has relied upon copy of his driving licence and exhibited the same as Ex. PW2/1.
9.
During his cross-examination on behalf of insurance company, he deposed that he was the eyewitness to the accident in question.

He denied the suggestion that at the time of accident,
deceased was riding the motorcycle at the wrong side of the road.
He further denied the suggestion that deceased Prashant was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.
He deposed that he had removed the deceased to the hospital.
He further deposed that he had requested a passerby who helped him in shifting the deceased to the hospital in his car.
He denied the suggestion that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of his motorcycle by deceased.

10. The careful perusal of testimony of aforesaid witness i.e. PW1 would go to show that the respondents more particularly insurance company has not been able to impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross- examination.
It is an undisputed fact that FIR No. 342/19 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS. Madanganj with regard to accident in question.
Copy of said FIR (which is part of criminal case record), would show that same was registered on 07.10.2019 (accident being caused on 06.10.2019 at about 10:15 AM) on the statement of PW2 himself.
Thus, FIR is shown to have MACP No. 201/20; FIR No. 342/19 DOD: 13.08.2024 been registered promptly and without any delay.
Hence, there is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioners herein.

11. Not only this, the respondent no. 1 namely Mohd. Ashfaq Assam (accused in State case) has been charge sheeted for the offences punishable U/s 279/304A IPC & 134/187 M.V. Act by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

Same would also point out towards rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
12.

It is pertinent to note that the respondent no.1/driver of offending vehicle was the other material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident has taken place.
However, he has preferred not to enter into the witness box.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1.
There is nothing on record to show that the petitioners had any enmity with the driver of the offending vehicle so as to falsely implicate him in this case.

15. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderence of probabilities that Sh. Prashant Mehta had sustained fatal injuries in the road accident which took place on 06.10.2019 at about 10:15 AM at Ajmer Road, 100 meter prior to Railway Line, Madanganj, District Ajmer, Rajasthan,
due to rash and negligent driving on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Thus, this issue is decided in favour of petitioners and against the respondents.
16. The petitioners who are claimants are the husband and three minor children of deceased.
It is evident that the petitioners have actually suffered monetary loss and mental agony due to death of deceased.
Accordingly, petitioners are entitled for just and fair compensation in the present case.

17. Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988 enjoins upon the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award MACP No. 201/20; FIR No. 342/19 DOD: 13.08.2024 determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.

The guiding principles for assessment of "just and reasonable compensation" in fatal case has been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in case titled as Smt. Anjali & Ors., Vs. Lokendra Rathod & Ors, in Civil Appeal No. 9014 of 202, decided on 06.12.2022 that: -
"The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, "MV Act") gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.

Section 168 of the MV Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation'
which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the applicant/s.

In Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.3, this Court has laid down as under:
"16."Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.
